<a id="mathematics-abelian-sheaves-finite-site"></a>

## Abelian sheaves on finite sites

Source: [mathematics_abelian_sheaves_finite_site.esk](../examples/mathematics_abelian_sheaves_finite_site.esk#L1). SHA-256: `1b516d970bf01f9ae7f7e65232bac390a8804c17b8034ba59ff3528978a70136`.

**Purpose:** Compare sheafification and cohomology routes on finite Alexandrov sites.

**Implemented algorithm:** Build rational restriction matrices, matching-family kernels, plus construction, pointwise limits and Cech/derived-limit complexes.

**Domain and parameters:** Pseudocircle and pseudo-2-sphere; constant Q, a nonseparated presheaf and a monodromy -1 local system.

**Arithmetic:** Exact rational linear algebra and kernel/rank computations over Q.

**Checks in the source:** Functor laws, separated/sheaf conditions, point-route dimensions and kernel/cokernel dimensions are checked; the sphere cover deliberately misses H² when it is not Leray.

**Limits:** Rational coefficients omit torsion. Dimensionwise checks of exactness/comparison must not be described as a machine proof of the general sheafification theorem.

**Prerequisites:** Built eshkol-run and stdlib; native JIT or AOT.

<a id="mathematics-alphatensor-3x3-gf2"></a>

## Rank-23 matrix multiplication over F₂

Source: [mathematics_alphatensor_3x3_gf2.esk](../examples/mathematics_alphatensor_3x3_gf2.esk#L1). SHA-256: `222712935cc60af1f734f817d22c2b6a8c9fbcca97e4d56d6bf383d2710b1006`.

**Purpose:** Verify a supplied public AlphaTensor factorization.

**Implemented algorithm:** Contract U/V/W integer bit masks by parity of bitwise intersections.

**Domain and parameters:** 3×3 matrices over F₂; all 9×9 pairs of matrix units; fixed rank 23 witness.

**Arithmetic:** Exact integers and reduction modulo 2.

**Checks in the source:** Basis-pair expansion agrees with matrix-unit multiplication; bilinearity extends this complete tensor identity to every pair of 3×3 F₂ matrices.

**Limits:** Certifies the supplied bilinear witness over F₂; does not search for it or prove rank optimality.

**Prerequisites:** Built eshkol-run and stdlib; native JIT or AOT.

<a id="mathematics-aoki-cycles-fermat-sextic"></a>

## Cycle supports on the Fermat sextic surface

Source: [mathematics_aoki_cycles_fermat_sextic.esk](../examples/mathematics_aoki_cycles_fermat_sextic.esk#L1). SHA-256: `2367ee5fcc98cde07590fce5085459b276442f35518dfc46e675ed720591b28e`.

**Purpose:** Measure which rational Hodge characters the supplied lines and two Aoki curve families cover.

**Implemented algorithm:** Expand sparse four-variable factorizations and Jacobian determinants in the exact extension tower; reduce in the Jacobian ring and close supports under permutations/Galois actions.

**Domain and parameters:** Degree-6 surface X₆²; lines, p=2,d=3 curve C and p=3,d=2 curve Y; 85 primitive Hodge characters.

**Arithmetic:** Exact Q(ζ₁₂)[c]/(c³−2) coefficients and integer exponents.

**Checks in the source:** Tower relations, polynomial decompositions, line supports, Galois closure and Hodge membership are asserted; a receipt records the uncovered support count.

**Limits:** A PASS receipt reports the computed gap for its parameters; it does not imply the gap is zero. Period and support conclusions use the cited geometric results.

**Prerequisites:** Built eshkol-run and stdlib; native JIT or AOT.

<a id="mathematics-aoki-cycles-fermat-surfaces-sweep"></a>

## Aoki cycle supports by surface degree

Source: [mathematics_aoki_cycles_fermat_surfaces_sweep.esk](../examples/mathematics_aoki_cycles_fermat_surfaces_sweep.esk#L1). SHA-256: `33d0a77acceb97ce29a75d0a70f659cd53c118e7d9c8d503094d257f6c77e56f`.

**Purpose:** Sweep the supports of available p-standard cycles against Fermat-surface Hodge characters.

**Implemented algorithm:** Construct degree-dependent cyclotomic/radical towers, verify polynomial decompositions and union line/C/Y/Q supports across divisor levels; organize residual character orbits and bounded multiset witnesses.

**Domain and parameters:** MATH_FERMAT_DEGREE defaults 8 (header domain m≥4); eligible C levels are even, Y levels divisible by 3 and Q levels divisible by 4; MATH_WITNESS_K defaults 4.

**Arithmetic:** Exact sparse polynomial and extension-field arithmetic.

**Checks in the source:** JSON receipt reports C/Y/Q support and cover counts, divisor levels, missing characters/orbits, bounded inductive witnesses and no-witness counts; PASS checks support/Hodge/Galois consistency, not zero missing count.

**Limits:** The Q-family decomposition is checked as an exact polynomial identity; the earlier modular screen was a discovery method. The bounded witness search reports no witness only within its configured bound, which does not imply that no algebraic cycle exists.

**Prerequisites:** Built eshkol-run and stdlib; native JIT or AOT.

<a id="mathematics-classifying-space-dijkgraaf-witten"></a>

## Finite-group classifying spaces and state sums

Source: [mathematics_classifying_space_dijkgraaf_witten.esk](../examples/mathematics_classifying_space_dijkgraaf_witten.esk#L1). SHA-256: `8f88b7dec7f8bc1362bd3c5b9d082a9c21b3c3ce5a5e99f90436a607ded6e172`.

**Purpose:** Connect explicit bar-complex homology, Q/Z cocycles and Dijkgraaf–Witten state sums.

**Implemented algorithm:** Build nerve boundary matrices and integer Smith forms; test cocycles/coboundaries, enumerate flat colorings of branched Delta-complexes and pair cocycles with fundamental cycles.

**Domain and parameters:** Z/2, Z/3, (Z/2)² and S₃ homology cases; state sums on the supplied S³, RP³ and T³ complexes with the implemented groups/twists.

**Arithmetic:** Exact bignum integer linear algebra, rational cocycles modulo 1 and exact sign phases.

**Checks in the source:** Homology and twist counts, untwisted connection counts, lens/commuting-triple formulas, RP³ fundamental-class pairing and a wrong-orientation negative control are checked.

**Limits:** Finite supplied complexes and group/twist sets delimit the computation; no universal classification of arbitrary manifolds or gauge groups is executed.

**Prerequisites:** Built eshkol-run and stdlib; native JIT or AOT.

<a id="mathematics-cohomology-rings-cup-products"></a>

## Cup products and Bockstein on finite-group nerves

Source: [mathematics_cohomology_rings_cup_products.esk](../examples/mathematics_cohomology_rings_cup_products.esk#L1). SHA-256: `76c92a5f354f0d6352bc980b035e2d41070495bdcc5c45b1987eee70131664bb`.

**Purpose:** Compute ring information beyond cohomology dimensions and identify selected Dijkgraaf–Witten twists.

**Implemented algorithm:** Normalized bar cochains, modular coboundary ranks, Alexander–Whitney cup products and Bockstein from integer lifts; Q/Z coboundary systems for cubic classes.

**Domain and parameters:** Z/2, Z/4, Z/3, (Z/2)² and (Z/2)³; selected products through degrees 3/4; all 127 nonzero combinations of seven surviving cubic twists.

**Arithmetic:** Exact arithmetic over F₂, F₃ and integers.

**Checks in the source:** Relations, independence, graded commutativity, Cartan/Bockstein comparisons and Q/Z twist nontriviality are asserted.

**Limits:** The finite degree computations support these stated relations; they are not an unlimited symbolic presentation proof for every degree or group.

**Prerequisites:** Built eshkol-run and stdlib; native JIT or AOT.

## Symmetric square, connected sums and second k-invariant

Source: [mathematics_cp2_symmetric_square_connected_sums.esk](../examples/mathematics_cp2_symmetric_square_connected_sums.esk#L1). SHA-256: `cd4208ffe43a2c638469407a77c56db2761be82d9c24f9ba8e489850eb395c1d`.

**Purpose:** Distinguish simply connected four-manifold models with equal mod-2 homology.

**Implemented algorithm:** Quotient the simplicial product of tetrahedron-boundary spheres by factor swap; glue connected sums by face tables; compute modular cohomology, cup forms and mapping-space state sums.

**Domain and parameters:** 10-vertex/48-pentachoron CP² Delta-complex; S²×S² and the supplied CP² connected sums; target π₂=π₃=Z/2 with k equal to cup square.

**Arithmetic:** Exact finite incidence data, F₂ ranks and rational state-sum weights.

**Checks in the source:** Cell counts, pseudomanifold/Euler/Betti checks, odd/even forms and state-sum versus fibration comparisons separate S²×S² from CP²#CP².

**Limits:** The quotient is a Delta-complex, not a simplicial complex or minimal triangulation. The topology identifications follow the cited source.

**Prerequisites:** Built eshkol-run and stdlib; native JIT or AOT.

<a id="mathematics-finite-categories-kan-extensions"></a>

## Finite categories and Kan extensions

Source: [mathematics_finite_categories_kan_extensions.esk](../examples/mathematics_finite_categories_kan_extensions.esk#L1). SHA-256: `d04c60d9390806909c63b23ddbb572074f467f00f796246942972bf33c88e117`.

**Purpose:** Make finite categorical constructions explicit and test their universal-property comparisons.

**Implemented algorithm:** Enumerate presented arrows/composites, functors, natural transformations, limits/colimits, comma-category Kan extensions and categories of elements.

**Domain and parameters:** Walking arrow, commutative square, pseudocircle/cone diagrams and Z/2 sets; finite derived-limit examples.

**Arithmetic:** Exact finite sets, arrow tables and rational/integer cochain linear algebra.

**Checks in the source:** Identity/composition/naturality laws, selected adjunction triangles, extension sizes, element-category lifting and derived-limit dimensions are checked.
